text:
anya: quick check — ran the spectral-cluster + recall@5 suite on sparkplug-v2-int6 across en/fr/de holdouts. getting a silhouette drop compared to v1, and recall@5 down ~4pts. anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

mike: can you paste the numbers and the exact eval config?

anya: sure, pasted run summary below (shortened):

```
model: sparkplug-v2-int6
holdouts: en/fr/de (10k each)
metrics:
  recall@1: 0.71 -> 0.68
  recall@5: 0.88 -> 0.84
  silhouette: 0.24 -> 0.15
  idflip_rate: 0.4% -> 3.2%
batching: 8
whitening: enabled (sparsity-aware)
quant: per-channel symmetric, 6-bit
```

mike: wow idflip up that much is concerning. was preprocessing identical? tokenization or embedding normalization changes? :eyes:

anya: preprocessing identical. I re-ran with whitening off and recall@5 improved ~1pt but silhouette still low.

siva: @anya can you run a centroid-delta check (L2 between v1/v2 centroids) per-cluster? my hunch is quantization bias shifting centroid norms for rare-token-heavy clusters.

anya: did that quick:

```
centroid_l2_delta (median): 0.098
centroid_l2_delta (90p): 0.27
notable: cluster 37 (de longtail) delta 0.62
```

karen: that matches a separate short test i ran on small multilingual subset — the longtail clusters have bigger norm changes. could be per-channel scale misestimated on low-activation channels.

siva: hmm. if scale per-channel is dominated by outliers in the calibration batch, rare-token channels get noisy scales -> heavier clipping/rounding. do we compute calibration on a stratified sample?

anya: calibration used 1000 random examples from en/fr/de pooled. not stratified, so longtail underrepresented.

mike: try recalib with stratified sampling (include more longtail examples) and also run a cosine-normalized eval (unit-norm embeddings) — that'll remove norm-shift effects from centroid deltas.

anya: running both now. quick experiment status:
- stratified-calib (n=2000) queued
- post-normalization run queued

eval-bot: summary report available: https://internal.eval/reports/1748027777 (contains per-cluster recall, centroid deltas, nearest-neighbor histograms) :white_check_mark:

karen: small nit — also check neighbor distance distributions (k=100) to see if quantization widens intra-cluster distances relative to inter-cluster. could explain silhouette drop.

anya: yup adding that to the report.

mike: if stratified recalib fixes it we should add a quick guard in the quant pipeline: default to stratified calibration for embedding tables (fallback to random only if sample pools < X). make a PR after you confirm.

anya: plan: (1) finish stratified recalib + unit-norm run (2) if improved, open PR to change calib sampling and add integration test (small synthetic longtail) (3) backfill failing holdouts and run canary. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

siva: thanks — ping me if you want me to inspect per-channel scales.

anya: thanks all, will update in ~30m. :coffee:
